Just hours after announcing Apple's support for wildfire victims in southern Europe, Tim Cook said the company would also donate to assist relief efforts following the earthquake in Kumamoto, Japan. Here are the details.

Apple will donate to support disaster relief efforts in Japan

Apple CEO Tim Cook once again took to social media platform X to announce the company's plans to assist communities affected by natural disasters.

Cook said the company is donating to support disaster relief in Japan, adding that the country "holds a very special place in my heart." You can read his full post below:

A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on Tuesday afternoon, with its epicentre located about 12 miles south of Kumamoto City. Currently, 34 people have died, thousands have been left homeless, and tens of thousands of households remain without water and power.

According to Reuters, ongoing aftershocks and extreme heat in the area have also made rescue and recovery efforts more difficult.

Cook's announcement came just hours after he said Apple would assist millions of wildfire victims in southern Europe, continuing Apple's tradition of stepping up in the face of natural disasters and other emergencies.

Apple also has an internal donation programme called "Employee Giving," which has raised over US$880 million to date through a donation matching policy.
